events.content:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

node server.js & PID=$!; sleep 0.5

node server.js & PID=$!; sleep 0.5
echo "--- after restart:"; curl -s localhost:3456/ | sed -n '/<h2>Currently/,/<h2 id/p'
kill $PID; cat /tmp/smoke/books.json

args.content:
# Reading list

A small app for keeping track of the books you're reading. No accounts, no database — books are saved to `data/books.json`.

```sh
npm start        # http://127.0.0.1:3000
npm test
```

Settings (environment variables):

- `PORT` — default `3000`
- `HOST` — default `127.0.0.1` (only this machine). Use `0.0.0.0` to let other people open your book links; note that anyone who can reach the app can also add books and mark them finished.
- `DATA_FILE` — default `data/books.json`

Each book has its own page at `/books/<id>`, and that's the link to send someone.

events.content:
The reading-list app is built and working. Run `npm start` and open http://127.0.0.1:3000. It uses plain Node with nothing extra to install.

I tested it two ways. The 14 automated tests pass (`npm test`). I also ran the real server: I added a book, opened its page, marked it finished, restarted the server, and the book was still there under "Finished".

**What it does**
- **Home page:** shows "Currently reading" and "Finished" (newest first, with the date you finished). Each book in progress has a **Mark finished** button, and the **Add a book** form is at the bottom. Title is required; author and notes are optional.
- **Book page:** each book has its own page at `/books/<id>` showing the title, author, whether you're reading it or finished it, and your notes (line breaks kept). That address is the link you send someone, and the page title reads "Title by Author" so it looks right when shared.
- **Saving:** books are stored in `data/books.json`, which git ignores. If the app crashes while saving, the old file stays intact. If the file is ever damaged, the app won't start rather than overwrite your data.

**Before you send links**
- **Where it runs:** by default the app only works on your own computer, so a link you send won't open for anyone else. For others to open links, it has to run somewhere they can reach, and be started with `HOST=0.0.0.0`.
- **No accounts:** anyone who can open the app can also add books and mark them finished, not just read them. That's fine on your own network, but worth knowing before putting it on the public internet.

Notes can only be written when you add a book; there's no way to edit them yet. If you want to keep notes as you read, editing them on the book page would be a small addition.

The code is in `server.js` (startup), `src/store.js` (saving to the JSON file), `src/app.js` (pages and actions), `src/views.js` (the HTML) and `test/app.test.js`. I haven't committed anything.
